expected_outcome: Verification and CI consumers derive outcomes from current canonical evidence and prove that tests executed.
observations: Regressions cover edited verification and CI stamps, forged session IDs, attacker-controlled downgrade text, zero executed tests, exit-zero failing JUnit, stale report reuse, unavailable counts, stale CI and brief state, non-finite trace values, policy command precedence, and workspace aggregation.
The post-Fable focused TR-3 suite reported 402 passed in 183.77 seconds.
Direct Fable installed-path cases reported 8 passed and the broader installed adversarial matrix reported 22 passed, each parameterized over plugin and bridge launch modes.
Counted pytest evidence binds collected, executed, passed, failed, errors, skipped, and portable argv in the canonical artifact.
A zero-count custom command remains UNKNOWN during the compatibility window; an all-skipped pytest run is a violation.
Effective policy owns the test command, full is the default verification scope, and explicit impacted scope remains partial.

Assurance and brief use canonical validators; all-skipped CI, edited ok fields, stale source, cross-repository pushes, local commits after push, and pushed commits without retained status remain non-pass.
